meta.title: East Liverpool in clay
meta.summary: Kilns helped shape East Liverpool. The Museum of Ceramics tells the story of the hands behind its pottery. ♡

sourceRefs.label: Ohio History Connection · Museum of Ceramics

blocks.text: East Liverpool grew into a major American pottery center, and its Museum of Ceramics displays wares made there while tracing the industry’s growth from the nineteenth into the twentieth century. A cup may look simple at first glance; then clay, skilled hands, firing, decoration, and the people around the kilns begin to emerge.

The museum also displays a mural of James Bennett’s early pottery. I’d linger over it, then look at the objects again: everyday things with a whole local economy behind them. Pick out a shape or a painted detail that catches your eye. That’s where I’d begin our conversation about how an object gets made. I’d look at a familiar shape—a cup or plate—and imagine the making behind it. A small object can keep me curious for quite a while. ♡
